title: The Club Plantation in Kansas City burns down, 1940
summary: The band and show open a Kansas City branch whose fancy food and small market fail, and it burns down about the fifth week.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: That's right. We opened up a Club Plantation in Kansas City. They opened up a club in Kansas City, in 1940. And we took the whole show and band up there, the whole Kitchen

Well, we stayed -- we opened up, had a nice crowd. And we had dinners on Sunday, we played dinner music, around about 6:00 on Sunday afternoon. And people came out there. But they tried to make a fine cafe out of it, but it wasn't that type of place. The food didn't come up to what they wanted it to be, see. If you're going to serve food, and get big prices for it, your cafe has got to have a certain character.

And you've got to -- it takes more than just money. You've got to use a lot of imagination. And you've got to have different chefs that can do various things to enhance a place like that, see. So we opened up and they had nightclub every night. And at first the crowds came, you know what I mean. But Kansas City was a much smaller town than St. Louis. And they just didn't keep the place up, see.
So one night the place burned down.
And Reuben was saying that we would noticed every night.
a little funny, but one of them guys said, (Unintelligible) look like you ought "Gee, it to be closing pretty soon." You used to hear things like that.
